```plato

    // The intersection of two sampled distances: the maximum. A lower bound:
    // outside a corner the larger of the two distances under-estimates the
    // distance to the corner itself.
    IntersectionDistance(a: Number, b: Number): Number
        => a.Max(b);

    // The first distance with the second subtracted from it: a against negated b.
    // A lower bound, being the intersection above.
    SubtractDistance(a: Number, b: Number): Number
        => a.Max(b.Negative);

    // The symmetric difference of two sampled distances: inside exactly one of
    // the two shapes. A lower bound — it is built from intersections.
    // (IQ: opXor.)
    ExclusiveOrDistance(a: Number, b: Number): Number
        => a.Min(b).Max(a.Max(b).Negative);

    // The polynomial smooth minimum of two distances, blended over blendRadius.
    // Reduces to the plain minimum as blendRadius approaches zero. A lower bound:
    // it mixes its operands with weights that sum to one and then subtracts, so
    // it never exceeds the plain minimum.
    // Precondition: blendRadius is positive. (IQ: opSmoothUnion.)
    SmoothUnionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, blendRadius: Number): Number {
        var h = (0.5 + 0.5 * (b - a) / blendRadius).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        return b.Lerp(a, h) - blendRadius * h * (1.0 - h);
    }

    // The smooth intersection: the smooth union of the negated distances,
    // negated. A lower bound, by the same weights-sum-to-one argument as the
    // smooth union. Precondition: blendRadius is positive.
    // (IQ: opSmoothIntersection.)
    SmoothIntersectionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, blendRadius: Number): Number
        => SmoothUnionDistance(a.Negative, b.Negative, blendRadius).Negative;

    // The smooth difference: a smoothly intersected with the complement of b.
    // A lower bound. Precondition: blendRadius is positive.
    // (IQ: opSmoothSubtraction.)
    SmoothDifferenceDistance(a: Number, b: Number, blendRadius: Number): Number
        => SmoothIntersectionDistance(a, b.Negative, blendRadius);

    // The complement of a shape: inside becomes outside, and the magnitude is
    // unchanged, so an exact operand stays exact. This is the one CSG operator
    // with no meaningful BOUNDED form — the complement of a bounded solid is
    // unbounded, so no conservative box can enclose its non-positive region,
    // which is why there is no Complement beside the Union / Intersection /
    // Difference wrappers above.
    ComplementDistance(a: Number): Number
        => a.Negative;

    // A linear morph from the first shape (t = 0) to the second (t = 1). Exact
    // only where the two operands agree; in between it is a lower bound, since
    // interpolating two distance functions does not interpolate their surfaces at
    // unit gradient.
    MorphDistance(a: Number, b: Number, t: Number): Number
        => a.Lerp(b, t);

    //==
    // Chamfered and exactly-filleted CSG.
    //
    // Two alternatives to the polynomial smooth operators above, for when the join
    // between two shapes is a specified DIMENSION rather than an aesthetic choice:
    // a 45-degree bevel, and a true circular arc. `SmoothUnionDistance` is cheaper
    // than either but its blend is a polynomial approximation of an arc, not an arc.
    //
    // Fidelity: every operator here measures against a bevel plane or an arc placed
    // at the seam, which is the true distance only where the two surfaces cross at
    // a right angle. A lower bound there and near it; as the two surfaces approach
    // PARALLEL the seam term inflates by up to sqrt(2) and stops being a bound at
    // all, so divide by that factor before marching a near-tangential join.

    // The union of two distances with a 45-degree chamfer of the given width across
    // the seam. The third term is the distance to the bevel plane, which cuts the
    // corner the plain minimum would leave. Precondition: width is positive.
    // (hg_sdf: fOpUnionChamfer.)
    ChamferUnionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, width: Number): Number
        => a.Min(b).Min((a + b - width) / Number.SqrtTwo);

    // The intersection of two distances with a 45-degree chamfer of the given width.
    // Precondition: width is positive. (hg_sdf: fOpIntersectionChamfer.)
    ChamferIntersectionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, width: Number): Number
        => a.Max(b).Max((a + b + width) / Number.SqrtTwo);

    // The first shape with the second chamfer-subtracted: chamfered intersection
    // against the complement. Precondition: width is positive.
    // (hg_sdf: fOpDifferenceChamfer.)
    ChamferDifferenceDistance(a: Number, b: Number, width: Number): Number
        => ChamferIntersectionDistance(a, b.Negative, width);

    // The union of two distances joined by a quarter-circle fillet of the given
    // radius — a true arc, unlike the polynomial SmoothUnionDistance.
    // Precondition: radius is positive. (hg_sdf: fOpUnionRound.)
    CircularUnionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, radius: Number): Number {
        var corner = Vector2D((radius - a).Max(0.0), (radius - b).Max(0.0));
        return radius.Max(a.Min(b)) - corner.Magnitude;
    }

    // The intersection of two distances joined by a quarter-circle fillet.
    // Precondition: radius is positive. (hg_sdf: fOpIntersectionRound.)
    CircularIntersectionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, radius: Number): Number {
        var corner = Vector2D((radius + a).Max(0.0), (radius + b).Max(0.0));
        return radius.Negative.Min(a.Max(b)) + corner.Magnitude;
    }

    // The first shape with the second subtracted, the cut filleted by a true arc.
    // Precondition: radius is positive.
    CircularDifferenceDistance(a: Number, b: Number, radius: Number): Number
        => CircularIntersectionDistance(a, b.Negative, radius);

    // The exponential smooth minimum of two distances. Unlike the polynomial
    // SmoothUnionDistance this operator is ASSOCIATIVE: blending three or more shapes
    // gives the same result in any order, where the polynomial form's answer depends
    // on how the operands were parenthesized. That is what it buys for the price of
    // two exponentials and a logarithm. A lower bound, like the polynomial form:
    // its operand weights sum to one. Precondition: blendRadius is positive.
    // (https://iquilezles.org/articles/smin/)
    ExponentialSmoothUnionDistance(a: Number, b: Number, blendRadius: Number): Number
        => ((a.Negative / blendRadius).Exp + (b.Negative / blendRadius).Exp).NaturalLog
           * blendRadius.Negative;

    //==
    // Joints between two surfaces.
    //
    // Operators whose result is a feature running ALONG the curve where two shapes
    // meet, rather than a modified version of either. All four take the second shape
    // as a cutting or guiding surface, not as a solid to be merged. Fidelity is the
    // chamfer family's above: a lower bound where the two surfaces cross at a right
    // angle or near it, and not a bound as they approach parallel.

    // A rounded pipe of the given radius running along the curve where the two
    // surfaces meet. (hg_sdf: fOpPipe.)
    PipeDistance(a: Number, b: Number, radius: Number): Number
        => Vector2D(a, b).Magnitude - radius;

    // The first shape carrying a V-shaped engraving of the given depth where the
    // second shape's surface crosses it. (hg_sdf: fOpEngrave.)
    EngraveDistance(a: Number, b: Number, depth: Number): Number
        => a.Max((a + depth - b.Abs) / Number.SqrtTwo);

    // The first shape carrying a rectangular groove where the second crosses it:
    // depth into the surface, halfWidth to either side. (hg_sdf: fOpGroove.)
    GrooveDistance(a: Number, b: Number, depth: Number, halfWidth: Number): Number
        => a.Max((a + depth).Min(halfWidth - b.Abs));

    // The first shape carrying a raised rectangular tongue where the second crosses
    // it — the mating half of a groove. (hg_sdf: fOpTongue.)
    TongueDistance(a: Number, b: Number, height: Number, halfWidth: Number): Number
        => a.Min((a - height).Max(b.Abs - halfWidth));
```
